relevance_note: Case series of one family with Danon disease and a LAMP2 frameshift variant: 'eight individuals [including the proband (Ⅲ-1)] were confirmed to have frameshift mutation secondary to a 2-bp deletion (c.257_258delCC) in the exon 3 of the LAMP2 gene'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script assembled the JSON and cut table spans from the Markdown table lines (row from the patient label through the cell); each cut was checked against the tables. Labels use the paper's Roman-numeral pedigree labels verbatim (Ⅱ-2 etc. as printed; I-1 as printed in the Figure 1 legend). Table 1 = baseline 2017; Tables 2 and 3 have one row per patient and CMR year (columns 'Case No. and Time' twice: label, then year). Scope: the 7 enrolled patients, plus Ⅳ-1 (asymptomatic 8-year-old boy excluded from the CMR study) and I-1 (pedigree legend: died of heart disease at 45). Variant attribution: the paper states 'eight individuals [including the proband (Ⅲ-1)] were confirmed to have' c.257_258delCC, then excludes Ⅳ-1 and 'Therefore' enrols the seven patients; it does not list the eight by name, so the variant rows for the six non-proband patients and Ⅳ-1 rest on this count, not on a per-person statement. No variant row for I-1 (generation I, not among the fourteen tested members of generations Ⅱ–Ⅳ). Zygosity, inheritance and parental testing are not stated for anyone. Ages: 'Age in 2017' is the baseline, not the last evaluation (follow-up ran to 2022), so last-evaluation age is given only for Ⅲ-1 (22, last CMR 2019, died at 22) and Ⅲ-6 (19, CMR 2022). Lab features were judged against the reference ranges printed in the Table 1 notes plus the text statements; ALT is not in the text's list of analysed markers, so ALT rows rest on the table values and reference range only. LVOT obstruction, RVWT and LVEF/LVEDd absences come from statements about the seven patients / 'remaining six cases' / 'other patients' (inferred from group statement). LGE absence for Ⅲ-2 and Ⅲ-5 is inferred: five patients with LGE are identified (four HCM + Ⅲ-4), and the text refers to 'the two patients without LGE'; the '/' cells in Table 2 are not defined. 'Normal' in the Table 1 'Intellectual disabilities' column was taken to exclude the composite intellectual/learning checklist item (that column records learning difficulty for Ⅲ-1 and Ⅲ-6) but not ADHD. Normal cardiac morphology (Ⅲ-2, Ⅲ-4, Ⅲ-5) was taken to exclude LVH. Contradictions/errors in the paper: (1) Ⅲ-5 AST 50 U/L is above the printed reference (15–46) but the text says only HBDH and LDH were elevated in the five females: both rows emitted, checklist liver enzymes 'not reported'. (2) 'Both IV-1 and IV-6 experienced cardiomyopathy with earlier onset during their second decade of life' and 'low T2 signal foci ... of patient IV-1 and IV-6' conflict with Ⅳ-1 being an asymptomatic 8-year-old and there being no IV-6 (apparently Ⅲ-1 and Ⅲ-6); not used for anyone. (3) 'Ⅱ-2, Ⅱ-3, and Ⅲ-2 manifest cardiomyopathy during adulthood' conflicts with Ⅲ-2 being 15 with onset N/A and normal morphology; not used. (4) Ⅲ-1 cause of death: text 'succumbed to heart failure', Figure 1 legend 'suddenly died of heart disease'; heart failure recorded with both spans. (5) Follow-up end given as both 'July 2022' and 'May 2022'. Ⅱ-2: LVEF normal at baseline (excluded) but 'mildly decreased' in 2019 (49.89%): both rows, checklist reduced-EF item 'not reported'. RV hypertrophy for Ⅲ-1/Ⅲ-6 uses the text 'RV free wall significantly thickened' / 'increased gradually' with Table 2 RVWT_max and the paper's >5 mm definition; baseline RVWT was normal for all seven. Ⅳ-1 'asymptomatic' recorded as no feature row (a whole-person statement excludes nothing specific). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients: set true because the proband's diagnosis sentence cites reference (13) (Cheng 2012, endomyocardial biopsy series); the paper does not say in words that he was reported there.
